name: INR/USD Exchange Rate
summary: USD/INR, Day 228. The rupee went through its stated 96.60 line — closes of 96.78, ~96.88 and 96.71 on 7–9 Oct after the RBI's hike failed to stop the slide — but the true record (96.96, May) held, and the graph's 96.60 anchor was mis-specified. On Saturday 10 Oct the RBI opened a window supplying the oil companies' entire daily dollar needs from reserves and imposed derivative curbs (no rebooking, $5mn hedging threshold, a 20% cash FX Risk Reserve); the rupee gained 93p on 12 Oct (95.78), its best day in six months, and traded ~95.3 on 13 Oct. Drivers: Brent >$100 and the $116–121 Indian basket, FPI outflows, US 10Y >5.2%, DXY at an 18-month high. Cost: reserves −$46bn in three weeks to $734.6bn, plus a ~$200bn net short forward book. Analysts: range 94–97 (Kotak), fair value 94.50–95 (Finrex). Tests: re-weakening through 96.50 with the window running (= not enough); a close below 95.00 (= floor credible); RBI withdrawing the window (the 2013 stabilisation tell).

recent_signals.headline: **THE RUPEE CAN'T FIRM DESPITE SUB-$100 OIL — RBI IS DEEP IN THE TOOLBOX YET THE RUPEE STILL WON'T HOLD ₹95 = A STRESS SIGNAL.** Operative: USD/INR ~₹95.68 (rupee ~₹95.70; -0.2% 1D, +1.1% MoM, +5.1% 3M vs ~₹87.9 pre-crisis). Even with operative Brent sub-$100 — the oil import-bill relief that 'should' help the rupee — the currency will not firm, because the binding constraint is record FII outflows (~₹3.33 lakh crore FY26, Republic World May 28) + 15-year-low FPI ownership, not the oil bill alone. **The macroprudential escalation is now stacked deep**: the $5B buy-sell swap auction (May), ~$1B/day spot dollar sales, NDF position controls (April 1 barred AD banks from offering rupee NDF to corporates; partial lift April 20), bank NOP capped ~$100M/day, and ~$700B reserves deployed. **When a central bank reaches this deep into the regulatory toolbox and the rupee STILL won't hold ₹95 on an oil-relief tape, that is the stress signal** — intervention can cap the currency but cannot reverse foreign positioning. Drivers (Business Standard): lingering US-Iran tension + foreign-fund outflows. **The organic ₹93-94 retracement still needs a SIGNED deal + Brent <$95 sustained + an FII turn**; a deal-break + Brent re-spike toward $115-120 reopens the ₹97-98 path despite intervention. **Regional comparator**: Iranian rial ~1,720,000 IRR/USD parallel market (no panic on the strikes); 2M hyperinflation trigger untriggered, ETA pushed further out. (NOTE: operative Brent ~$99, NOT the yfinance roll artifact.)

recent_signals.headline: **THE RUPEE STRENGTHENED on Friday — USD/INR 96.27, -0.4%** — off the record low of 96.52 close / 96.60 intraday around 14 July, on measured RBI intervention plus the risk-on tape. Reserves ROSE $964mn to **$675.157bn** for the week ended 10 July (FCA +$930mn to $546.508bn), confirming 'reserves intact'. **Two things the graph must catch: (1) reserves peaked at $728.494bn in the week ended 27 February, so the war has cost ~$53bn of reserves, about 7.3% of the peak; (2) this print covers the week ended 10 July and therefore does NOT capture the 13-17 July intervention around the record low — that defence shows up in the WSS released Friday 24 July, THE SAME DAY AS THE TARIFF CLIFF.** RBI Governor Malhotra (17 Jul) called the rupee 'relatively stable compared with global peers' — at a record low, a deliberately relaxed framing that should be read as **RBI signalling tolerance for the LEVEL while smoothing the PATH.** REJECTED as uncorroborated: a circulating 'record low 96.96' print and a '$681bn one-year low' reserves figure, both inconsistent with confirmed data. CONFIRMED.

**The record is being TOUCHED in real time — ₹96.53 late session (22 Jul), after opening 96.34-96.36.** The 96.52/96.60 record of ~14 July is being REACHED, not cleanly breached; the rupee gave up early gains as the oil rally to $94 intensified. The RBI is holding the line AT the record with $20.72bn of borrowed dollars (swap/FCNR(B)) and is reportedly CUTTING its FX forward book rather than spending spot reserves, while briefing Reuters it is debating LIMITING intervention. **The defence is being tested precisely at the level it was designed to hold, on a day oil made a war-restart high. Watch the 24 July reserves release (same day as the cliff) — it will flatter the underlying spot defence.** CONFIRMED.

**The record HELD — ~96.48-96.54 (23 Jul), defended, NOT cleanly broken past 96.60.** After touching the 96.52/96.60 record intraday 22 Jul, the rupee recovered ~5 paise on RBI support at the 23 Jul open, then drifted back to ~96.54 as oil rallied toward $100. The RBI is holding the line AT the record with $20.72bn of borrowed dollars and is CUTTING its record ~$104bn net-short forward book. **The defence is being held precisely at its design level for a fourth session on a war-restart-high oil day; the clean-break trigger (>96.60 held 3 sessions) has NOT fired.** No '96.96' or sub-96 breakout appeared — reject any such print.
